correctness.rationale: The leave-one-out mean is \(\bar Y-d_i/(n-1)\) and its residual is \(n|d_i|/(n-1)\), giving the stated jackknife+ endpoints. For a candidate offset \(x=y-\bar Y\), fresh symbolic expansion verifies exactly \(((n+1)d_i-x)^2-n^2x^2=(n+1)(n-1)(d_i-x)(x+c_nd_i)\). Therefore the candidate residual is no larger than training residual i exactly when y lies in the corresponding endpoint interval. Every such interval contains \(\bar Y\), so the points lying in at least \(j=\lfloor\alpha(n+1)\rfloor\) intervals form one interval with endpoints \(\ell_{(j)}\) and \(u_{(n-j+1)}\); the integer identity \(n-j+1=\lceil(1-\alpha)(n+1)\rceil\) gives exact equality. Exact-rational spot checks independently matched full-conformal membership, including the infinite-interval convention.

evidence: Barber et al. prove assumption-free jackknife+ coverage at least \(1-2\alpha\) and full-conformal coverage at least \(1-\alpha\).
Amann discusses asymptotic conditional-coverage relationships under stability.

value.rationale: The intercept-only location model is the canonical exact benchmark for regression conformal methods. Showing that jackknife+ recovers full conformal samplewise—thereby improving its generic worst-case guarantee from \(1-2\alpha\) to the full conformal grid in this model—clarifies a real boundary between the two procedures and supplies a clean test case for approximation and stability theory.
residual_risks: The identity is elementary enough that it may exist as folklore, lecture notes, or an unindexed exercise in conformal prediction.

final_claim: For intercept-only least squares with absolute residuals and the Barber–Candès–Ramdas–Tibshirani finite-sample quantile convention, jackknife+ and full conformal return exactly the same prediction set for every realized sample and every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\); the common set has the stated order-statistic endpoints, hence exchangeable coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) and exact grid coverage when augmented residuals are almost surely distinct.
limitations: The equality is specific to the sample-mean predictor and absolute-residual conformity score.
It does not extend by this proof to covariate-dependent least squares, ridge, nonlinear models, or arbitrary conformity scores.
Coverage is marginal under exchangeability, not training-conditional.
